headline: Stocks ripped on the midterms, chips and data-center names broke, and December hike odds sit near 80%.
regime: Hiking regime: the Fed raised rates in September and CME FedWatch puts roughly 77-82% odds on another 25bp hike on Dec 9. In this regime good economic news can be bad for stocks, and yields matter more than usual.

lean.t: Mixed: Dow futures up, Nasdaq futures down
lean.why: Dow futures were up about 0.5% and Nasdaq 100 futures down about 0.5-0.7% on Qualcomm and Asian chip weakness. Three Fed speakers today and jobs data Friday. Trade levels.

lean.t: Slight upward lean, hinges on jobs and CPI
lean.why: A hike is mostly priced in, so a soft jobs or CPI print that cools hike odds is the bullish surprise. A hot print pushes the 10-year back toward 5% and hurts rate-sensitive groups.

Stocks have risen from late October to April after all 19 midterms since 1950 (average 14.8%), but hiking-cycle windows gained about half that. AI spending faces political scrutiny, and the semiconductor index is at its lowest close since Apr 28.

rates.n: Held Oct 28, 10-2 vote; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike
CME FedWatch 82% (Discovery Alert, Nov 5), 80.7% (Finimize); 76.9% on Nov 4 (TokenPost)
Freddie Mac survey of Oct 29, down 8bp from 7.32%. The Nov 5 survey was not found, so this is a week old
Dec futures $4,073 at Nov 4 close (+3.4%); spot $4,134.83 on Nov 5

sectors.why: Democratic control keeps federal clean-energy support alive. First Solar rose 4.63% on Nov 4. Gridlock caps new laws, and spikes like this often give back some of the gain.
The sector rose 3.04% to a record. Centene +13%, HCA and Universal Health +10% on Medicaid and ACA hopes. CVS fell about 13% on its split plan, so this is a stock-picker's group.
Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%; GD, Northrop and RTX also fell. Defense budgets have usually been bipartisan, so deep cuts are less likely than headlines suggest.

Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -3.1% to its lowest close since Apr 28; Vertiv -12.9%, Constellation -6.7%. Qualcomm fell after hours and Kospi -4.8% today. Hyperscalers (Microsoft, Amazon, Apple) rallied.
Financials rose 3.46% to a record, the best day since April 2025. Card issuers (Synchrony, Capital One) fell on a possible rate cap.
The 10-year is 4.89%, and the Oct 29 Freddie Mac survey was 7.24%, still above 7%. A fall in the 10-year is the only fast fix.
Gold rose 3.4% to $4,073 on Nov 4 and about $4,135 on Nov 5 as the dollar and yields fell. Citi sees $4,500 in 3 months. After a 3% day, wait for pullbacks to the $4,000 area.
Energy sector -4.77% (second-worst day since April 2025) as WTI fell 8.3% to $88. Lower oil helps airlines and shippers and hurts drillers.
Russell 2000 rose 1.58% to 2,856.96 on Nov 4. Small caps borrow short, so they are the most sensitive to hike odds, for better or worse.
SpaceX closed Nov 4 at $135.92 (-3.81%), Tesla was -4.9% premarket and Trump Media -11% early. Trump Media is volatile, so size it small.
Power producers fell hard on data-center worries (Vistra and NRG about -14%), while rate-sensitive REITs trade with the 10-year. A fall in yields helps them, a spike over 5% hurts.
GEO -6.7% and CoreCivic -5.2%. Both had rallied on the immigration crackdown that a new Congress could oversee.

news.head: Fed hike odds near 82% for Dec 9; Hammack, Barkin and Logan speak today
news.mean: CME FedWatch put the odds of a December hike at about 82% (80.7% at Finimize, up from 77.4%). The Fed raised to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16 and held Oct 28 by 10-2, with Cook and Hammack wanting a hike. Hammack speaks at 8:50 ET, Barkin at 9:10 and Logan at 7:00 pm.
react: Bond proxies lose when yields rise
news.hist: Stockdads (Nov 4) found that windows with a Fed hiking cycle (1994, 2018, 2022) gained 9.0%, 8.6% and 7.7% from late October to April, about half the average midterm window.
news.today: Hawkish Fed talk plus a hot jobs print is the setup that sends the 10-year back toward 5%. Watch 8:50 and 9:10 ET.
news.later: Quality banks tend to hold up when rates rise. A lasting oil drop, which Citi says could turn the Fed toward cuts, is the main thing that would change this.

news.head: Democrats win Congress: Dow +3.03% in its best day since April 2025
news.mean: The Dow rose 1,569 points to 53,356, the S&P 500 gained 1.58% to 7,688.62 and the Nasdaq 1.44% to 25,736.51. Analysts say divided government lowers the odds of sweeping new laws. Trump said he would "just veto everything" if Democrats do not work with him.
react: Sector hit a record on Medicaid and ACA hopes
news.hist: Stockdads: the S&P 500 rose from the last close of October to the last close of April after all 19 midterms since 1950, averaging 14.8% (median 15.2%), with an average 7.1% pullback along the way.
news.today: Big one-day gaps often chop afterward. Trade levels, not the gap.
news.later: The midterm history is favorable, but hiking-cycle windows gained about half as much.

news.head: AI chips and data-center power sell off; Philadelphia Semiconductor Index -3.1%
news.mean: The chip index fell to its lowest close since Apr 28. Vistra and NRG dropped about 14%, Micron and Sandisk 7-8%, Nvidia about 3%, with Democrats expected to tighten data-center rules. Hyperscalers rallied: Microsoft about +7%, Amazon about +6%, Apple about +5%. Constellation fell 6.7% and Vertiv 12.9% (Alpha Vantage).
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy-driven drops in a strong-order-book group often retrace part of the move, but a moratorium headline can restart the selling.
news.today: Expect volatility in power and chip names. Do not average down without a level.
news.later: Order books (Vertiv Q3 sales +61%, GE Vernova backlog $197B per Motley Fool) are strong; the open question is regulation.

news.head: Data-center stocks plunge after midterms: Modine -24%, Sterling -20%, Comfort Systems -16%
news.mean: Vertiv fell 12.71% and GE Vernova 10.84% on the same day. In Texas, Gina Hinojosa beat Gov. Abbott after campaigning for a data-center moratorium, and Goldman expects conditional moratoria in TX, GA and MI.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: a policy shock hits the whole group first, then the stronger order books recover first.
news.today: Watch whether VRT and GEV hold the Nov 4 lows.
news.later: The writer suggests staging purchases of GEV and VRT rather than buying at once.

news.head: Oil drops about 8% in a day: WTI settles near $88, Brent $94.62
news.mean: WTI fell 8.3% and Brent 8.7%, its lowest since Sep 4, after a JD Vance post linking GOP losses to the Iran war raised hopes of a peace deal. The energy sector fell 4.77%, its second-worst day since April 2025. Brent was up about 1% on Nov 5 per Reuters.
react: Energy stocks fell more than 15% over a four-day oil slide
news.hist: Rule of thumb: oil drops from war-premium highs often reverse on a single headline.
news.today: Oil is headline-driven. Keep stops wide or stand aside.
news.later: Citi argues a lasting Hormuz reopening could turn the Fed toward cuts, which would help growth stocks.

news.head: Health care hits a record: Centene +13%, HCA +10%, but CVS -13% on a split plan
news.mean: The sector rose 3.04% to a record on hopes Congress delays Medicaid cuts and extends ACA subsidies. CVS fell about 13% on a plan to split into two companies by 1H 2028, while raising 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $8.20.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: policy hopes can fade if the bills do not move; gridlock can stall them too.
news.today: Stock-pickers market: the group is split by company.
news.later: Watch for actual Medicaid and ACA subsidy votes.

news.head: Defense stocks fall: Lockheed -7%, L3Harris -6%
news.mean: Investrade lists General Dynamics, Lockheed, Northrop and RTX as down too. The worry is a smaller defense budget under a Democratic Congress.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: defense budgets have usually been bipartisan, so deep cuts are less likely than headlines suggest.
news.today: Fading a politics-driven gap down is a judgment call.
news.later: Backlogs are long; budgets move slowly.

news.head: Financials +3.46% to a record, but card issuers fall on a possible rate cap
news.mean: It was the sector's best day since April 2025. Synchrony, Capital One and Bread Financial fell on a possible credit-card rate cap, and Trump earlier floated a 10% cap (Investrade).
news.hist: In the last three hiking cycles, JPMorgan rose in all three (+22.6%, +57.7%, +16.8%), but Bank of America fell 24.8% in 2022-23.
news.today: Card issuers are headline-sensitive; size small.
news.later: Quality banks are the cleanest hiking-cycle play, but it is not automatic.

news.head: Gold jumps 3.4% to about $4,073, then higher near $4,135-4,144 on Nov 5
news.mean: Dec gold closed Nov 4 at $4,073 (+3.37%), its biggest gain since August, as yields and the dollar fell. Spot was $4,134.83 on Nov 5 per Discovery Alert. Citi's scenario is $4,500 in 3 months and $5,000 in 6-12 months.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: after a 3% day, gold often retests the breakout level.
news.today: Pullbacks toward the $4,000 area are the levels to watch.
news.later: Citi's targets are one forecast, not a given.

news.head: October jobs report Friday: consensus +65k, 4.2% unemployment, wages +0.3%
news.srcN: TD Economics; Reuters poll via Discovery Alert, Nov 5
news.mean: September payrolls were +29k. ADP private payrolls rose 86,000 in October vs 69,000 expected, and ISM services was 54.5 with prices paid at 73.0. Stockdads says a 0.4% or higher wage print would make a December hike "a done deal."
news.hist: Rule of thumb: in a hiking regime, good economic news can be bad for stocks.
news.later: A cold print would revive growth stocks unless it raises recession fear.

news.head: Inflation: October CPI lands Tue Nov 10, and December hike odds hang on it
news.mean: August CPI was 3.4% y/y (energy +16.3%). No consensus for October had been published yet. Oil fell 8% on Nov 4, but that does not show up until the November data.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: core CPI matters more than the headline for the Fed.

news.head: Earnings movers: AppLovin +22.6% after hours, Qualcomm -7.2%, Snap -11.5%
news.mean: AppLovin guided Q4 revenue to $2.365B-$2.395B vs $2.25B expected and added a $3.2B buyback. Qualcomm's handset revenue fell 26%. Snap will stop reporting daily users. Reuters had Qualcomm down 10.1% and Snap down 10.1% premarket, with AppLovin up 16.4%.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: after-hours moves often change by the open.
news.later: Single quarters rarely change a long-term thesis.

news.head: Asian chip selloff: Kospi -4.8%, SK Hynix -9%; Bank of England expected to hike to 4.0%
news.mean: Samsung fell 6.7% and the Kospi is down about 40% from its June peak. Shanghai rose 3.6% and the Hang Seng 3%. The BoE decision is at 12:00 GMT; a hike from 3.75% to 4.00% would be its first in over three years.
news.hist: Rule of thumb: chip selloffs in Asia often hit US chips at the open.
news.later: A global hiking cycle is a headwind for long-duration growth.

calendar.t: Fed: Hammack 8:50, Barkin 9:10, Logan 7:00 pm; jobless claims and Q3 productivity 8:30 ET
calendar.usual: Fed tone moves hike odds. Claims near 194-196k keep the labor market looking firm.

calendar.t: Bank of England decision (12:00 GMT, hike to 4.00% expected)
calendar.usual: A hike is priced in; a hold would be a surprise for the pound.
Consensus +65k, 4.2%, wages +0.3% m/m. Big moves in yields, dollar and banks.
Tests the data-center power and space themes after the Nov 4 drop.
The key input to December's hike. Core matters more than the headline.

scen.title: What if Friday's jobs number is...

out: Mixed to lower; growth and small caps worst
Relief; focus moves to CPI Nov 10
Growth and small caps rally, unless recession fear takes over

playbook: Homebuilders, REITs, utilities, small caps and unprofitable growth are pressured first. Banks and the dollar hold up better.
Housing, small caps, growth and gold benefit. Mortgage rates ease a few weeks later.
Gold and miners, emerging markets and big multinationals gain. Importers lose.
Airlines, cruise lines and shippers win. Energy stocks lose. Headline inflation eases.
A growth and small-cap rally is the usual response. Banks lose some margin tailwind.
Bonds rally, defensives (healthcare, staples, utilities) lead. Cyclicals and banks get hit by recession worries.
